cards.explanation: The answer is earth. Job says, "Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore." (Job 28:2) So the metals come out of the ground. Getting them takes real digging, friends, like me going to the bottom of the chocolate chip bin.

The answer is True. Job says, "Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses for ore in deepest darkness." (Job 28:3) The miner goes where it's darkest and keeps going. That's a whole lot of nerve for a little ore.

The answer is far from where people live. Job says, "Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man." (Job 28:4) No neighbors, no foot traffic, nobody waving hello. Just the miner and his shaft.

The answer is sapphires with flecks of gold. Job says, "Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold." (Job 28:6) Two treasures in one spot, friends. That's like finding chocolate chips AND butterscotch bits in the same cookie.
The answer is False. Job says, "Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it." (Job 28:8) Not the falcon, not the lion. The king of the jungle never made it down that path.

The answer is True. Job says the miner "…hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure." (Job 28:10) Down in the dark, he still sees what's valuable. Friends, I can't even spot my own spatula on a clean counter.

The answer is light. The miner stops up the streams "…to bring what is hidden to light." (Job 28:11) Hidden things dragged out into the open. I spent years hidden in the back of a junk drawer before I was brought into the light, so this verse hits home.

The answer is value. Job says, "No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living." (Job 28:13) We just heard about all that silver and gold, friends, and wisdom is worth more than any of it. Nobody can put a price tag on it.

The answer is False. Job says, "…nor is it found in the land of the living." (Job 28:13) You can't just wander around and bump into it. Hang on, friends, because Job has more to say about where it is.
The answer is False. Job says, "It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver." (Job 28:15) You can't pay for it, no matter how big the pile. Wisdom doesn't take cash.

The answer is that they've heard a rumor about it. Job says, "Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’" (Job 28:22) Abaddon is a name for the place of destruction. Even they only caught a whisper.
The answer is understands. Job says, "But God understands its way, and He knows its place." (Job 28:23) Everything else came up empty, friends, and then comes the big turn. God knows.

The answer is that He sees everything under the heavens. Job says, "For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens." (Job 28:24) The ends of the earth and everything under the heavens are in His view. That's why He knows where wisdom is.

The answer is that He looked at it and established it. Job says, "…then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out." (Job 28:27) This happened right when God set up the wind, the waters and the rain. Wisdom was part of the picture.

The answer is the fear of the Lord. Job says God told man, "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom…" (Job 28:28) After all that digging and searching, friends, the answer was right there. No shovel needed.

The answer is True. God says, "…and to turn away from evil is understanding." (Job 28:28) So wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and understanding is turning away from evil. Two short lines, friends, and that's the whole answer.
